To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Fe deficiency alters mitochondrial ultrastructure and functionality, as revealed by a 3D analysis of the organelle.
Fe deficiency induces a significant increase in the volume and number of cristae in cucumber mitochondria.
Fe deficiency causes ultrastructural modifications in cucumber leaf mitochondria, as revealed by electron tomography.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ultrastructural modifications occurring in mitochondria from cucumber leaves under Fe deficiency, which are correlated to a metabolic status characterized with a reduced respiratory activity.
the study of the ultrastructural modifications occurring in cucumber leaf mitochondria under Fe deficiency and with the characterization of their biochemical changes.
the ultrastructure and the function of the mitochondria in cucumber leaves under different Fe nutritional conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ultrastructural changes occurring in cucumber mitochondria under Fe deficiency are consistent with the hypothesis that the plant cells are able to sense and adapt their metabolism in response to Fe deficiency.

the ultrastructural and biochemical changes occurring in cucumber leaf mitochondria during Fe starvation are consistent with the hypothesis of a role for these organelles as Fe sensing and signalling centres.
mitochondria play an active role in the sensing and signaling of Fe deficiency in plants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mitochondria are not only involved in the Fe sensing but also in the Fe signalling in plants.

the 3D reconstruction by TEM tomography of the ultrastructural modifications occurring in cucumber leaf mitochondria under Fe-deficient conditions, provides a new insight into the role of these plant organelles during Fe deficiency.

the ultrastructural modifications occurring in plant mitochondria, as revealed by TEM tomography and correlated with biochemical changes, might be involved as part of the plant Fe deficiency responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mitochondria are not only the main source of ATP in the plant cell, but they are also able to respond to the Fe status of the plant by changing their ultrastructure and functionality.
mitochondria are a dynamic organelle, which is continuously adapting to changes in their environment.
mitochondria are not only involved in the Fe sensing and signalling pathways, but they can also be considered a target of the Fe deficiency response.
